Internet firms are repositioning themselves by (1) focusing on their core competencies and (2) by developing new business models that are more closely tied to profitability.

Internet firms have morphed in three distinct ways: by (1) changing their business models, (2) acquiring other firms to change their product lines, and (3) acquiring other firms in an effort to change their business models.

the question of how Internet companies are adapting to the new economy and what this means for the evolution of the industry.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the "morphing" of Internet companies in the late 90s and early 2000s was a strategic and organizational phenomenon that is best characterized by a rapid, hyper-evolutionary, profitability-driven process of strategic repositioning and organizational re-factoring that was triggered by a sudden, massive, and unprecedented shift in industry dynamics.
the Internet companies that survived and thrived were the ones that were able to adapt their strategy and organizational structures to the new realities of the "new" new economy.
the most effective strategies in this period were those that were focused on profitability and return on investments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Internet economy's rapid ascent and equally rapid fall has resulted in a new set of strategic and organizational behaviors that are not yet well understood.
the "new" new economy is characterized by a high level of strategic reorientation and organizational change.
the Internet economy is a dynamic, evolving, and complex system that has been in a state of flux since its inception.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although many Internet companies have successfully adapted to the new economic realities of the Internet economy, there are still many that are struggling to find the right formula for success.
the Internet economy is a highly dynamic environment, where firms are continually adapting their strategies and organizations to changing conditions.
